explanation: I found no Mathlib lemma saying that the sorted eigenvalues `hS.eigenvalues hn` equal the antitone list of eigenvalues of an arbitrary orthonormal eigenbasis. I read `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Spectrum.lean`. It has `eigenvalues_antitone`, `exists_eigenvalues_eq`, `card_filter_eigenvalues_eq`, `charpoly_eq`, `sort_roots_charpoly_eq_eigenvalues` and `eigenvalues_eq_eigenvalues_iff` (equal eigenvalues ↔ equal characteristic polynomials), but no uniqueness statement of this kind. I also grepped all of Mathlib for statements of the form `eigenvalues hn … =`; the other hits (in Trace, Positive and SingularValues) are unrelated. Getting the result from the charpoly lemmas would take several steps: compute the charpoly in the basis `w`, then argue about sorted roots. That is more than a short glue derivation. Mathlib also has no Courant–Fischer characterisation that this could be a special case of.
